xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF from GitHub issue #2538 (swarm cohort fix-2606-2601-2530-2538-2540)

plan.title: doctor(payload-staleness): branch pin with stale tag must not false-nudge newer-release

narratives.Description: When VERSION ref is a moving branch but tag still holds a prior semver, payload-staleness under --network uses (tag || ref) for release applicability while git ls-remote verifies ref. A matching branch SHA no longer short-circuits, so npm comparison can emit a false newer-release finding.
narratives.Overview: Under --network, (tag || ref) for release applicability + git ls-remote on ref can false-nudge npm newer-release when install tracks a branch. Prefer ref when ref is not a publishable tag; ignore stale tag for branch pins.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator on a branch-pinned install, I want doctor payload-staleness not to suggest latest solely because of a stale tag field, so that branch-tracking installs are not falsely nudged to upgrade.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Adjust packages/core/src/doctor/payload-staleness.ts applicability to prefer non-tag ref / skip release-availability when ref is a branch.
2. Add regression fixture in doctor tests: branch ref + stale tag must not emit false newer-release.
3. CHANGELOG entry. Closes #2538.
narratives.Acceptance: Branch pin + stale tag does not emit false newer-release; tag pins still work; tests cover the case.

items.title: Prefer ref for applicability when ref is not a publishable tag

narrative.Acceptance: Given VERSION with ref=main|master and tag=stale semver, when payload-staleness runs with network, then it does not emit a false newer-release finding based on the stale tag.

items.title: Regression test for branch pin + stale tag

narrative.Acceptance: Given a fixture with branch ref and stale tag, when the doctor payload-staleness suite runs, then the false-nudge case is asserted.

expected_outputs: No false newer-release for branch pins with stale tag
